title: feat(geometry): chain 2D sketch primitives into loops with stable ids and nesting
body:
## What changed

New module `camcraft-geometry::sketch_chains` (issue #1861, part of the DXF chain #1452). One call:

```rust
pub fn chain(primitives: &[LayeredPrimitive], options: ChainOptions) -> Result<SketchChains, ChainError>
```

It takes the DXF reader's lines, arcs and circles (#1860, merged as #1937) in millimetres and returns `closed` loops, `open` chains and `rejected` primitives.

- **Joining.** Curve ends within the join tolerance (default 0.01 mm, allowed 1e-5 to 10 mm) are joined, per layer. A wider gap is never bridged: the chain stays open and reports its two free ends. A bridged gap is reported as `max_gap`.
- **Arc metadata survives.** A chain segment is the input primitive turned to the walk direction (`reversed`, start angle and sweep sign rewritten). Nothing is flattened or snapped.
- **Stable `ChainId`.** Closed loops are walked counterclockwise from their lowest joint, open chains from their lower end. The id is the 128-bit FNV-1a hash of the layer name and the curves in that order, quantized to 1e-6 mm. It does not depend on draw order or direction.
- **Outer or hole.** Depth is counted by an exact crossing-number test against the arcs. Even depth is `Outer`, odd is `Hole`, with the innermost container as `parent`. This is the even-odd rule of `geo2d::Region`.
- **Named refusals, per chain.** `DuplicatePrimitive`, `DegenerateSegment`, `Branch { at, degree }`, `SelfCrossing { at }`, `ZeroArea`, `DuplicateChain`. Closed chains that cross or touch each other keep their geometry but get `NestingAmbiguous` instead of a role, and so does every loop inside one of them. `SketchChains::strict()` turns the first of these into an `Err`.
- **Hard errors.** A bad tolerance, a non-finite, out-of-range or invalid primitive, and a drawing over the limits (coordinates below 1e7 mm, 2,000,000 primitives, 200,000,000 pair tests) return `Err`. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the module.

No new dependency, no file I/O, no ECS. No user-facing command is added, so there is no MCP tool in this PR; the import command and its tool are #1862.

## Algorithms and sources (clean room)

| Step | Source |
|---|---|
| End clustering on a grid | Bentley, Stanat and Williams, 1977 |
| Clusters and components | Tarjan, union-find, 1975 |
| Identity hash | FNV-1a, IETF draft-eastlake-fnv |
| Candidate pairs for the crossing search | Sweep and prune: Cohen, Lin, Manocha and Ponamgi, 1995; axis choice from Ericson, 2005 |
| Segment, line-circle and circle-circle contacts | O'Rourke, 1998; Schneider and Eberly, 2003 |
| Containment | Crossing number: Shimrat, 1962; Haines, 1994 |
| Loop area with arcs | Green's theorem |

Each submodule carries its provenance line. No vendor code, file or output was consulted. Decisions, alternatives dropped and known limits are in `docs/decisions/1861-sketch-chaining.md`.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green, 10 steps, 0 failed, 30.2 min (head 3c65e18a2). A geometry change makes quick run the batch plan, so that is every debug suite plus clippy.

Pinning tests, 18 in three new suites under `crates/geometry/tests/`:

- `sketch_chains.rs`
  - `unordered_lines_chain_into_one_counterclockwise_loop`
  - `chain_id_ignores_draw_order_and_direction_but_not_layer_or_geometry` (pins the id value; I recomputed it independently outside Rust)
  - `arc_metadata_survives_chaining`
  - `gap_wider_than_tolerance_stays_open_and_is_reported`
  - `open_chain_of_lines_and_arcs_starts_at_its_lower_end`
  - `arcs_that_close_a_circle_and_tangent_fillets_are_clean_loops`
  - `dxf_polyline_bulges_and_circles_chain_with_their_arcs` (through `dxf::parse`; same id as the loose primitives)
- `sketch_chains_nesting.rs`
  - `nested_rectangles_and_circles_classify_as_outer_and_hole` (compared with `geo2d::Region`)
  - `containment_follows_the_arcs_not_their_chords`
  - `shuffled_nests_of_mixed_shapes_keep_their_depth_and_parent` (200 seeded nests, rotated, shuffled, flipped)
  - `long_loop_chains_in_bounded_time` (40,000-side loop; 50,000-segment tall strip that pins the sweep axis)
- `sketch_chains_refusals.rs`
  - `self_crossing_loop_is_refused_by_name`
  - `branching_vertex_is_a_named_diagnostic`
  - `degenerate_pieces_are_refused_by_name`
  - `invalid_input_is_an_error_not_a_panic`
  - `crossing_loops_get_no_outer_or_hole_reading`
  - `dense_drawing_is_refused_within_the_work_limit`
  - `random_grid_sketches_never_panic_and_do_not_depend_on_input_order` (400 seeded sketches; every primitive chained or rejected once; depth checked against flattened polygons; accepted loops pass `Region::new`)

## What was not exercised

- No real-world DXF file was chained; inputs are hand-built or generated, plus one DXF text through the reader.
- Two curves that meet at a tangent cusp can read as `SelfCrossing` when rounding makes them cross away from the joint. Fillets and S-curves are pinned as clean; the cusp case is not.
- Open chains are not tested for self-crossing, by decision.
- Nothing calls `chain()` yet: the ECS entity, the project file and the import command are #1862.
- Debug-build timing only; the release lanes were not run.

Process change: no

Changelog: Sketch chaining in camcraft-geometry: DXF lines, arcs and circles join within a tolerance into closed loops and open chains with stable ids, arcs kept analytic, outer-versus-hole nesting, and named refusals for branches, self-crossing loops and degenerate pieces (#1861)

Effort: max (not escalated in this run; raised from high by the earlier attempt)

Fixes #1861

title: fix(c-axis): support -Z C rotary sense and arcs in stamp_c (slice 3)
body:
## What changed

- Interpret C rotary `"axis": [0, 0, -1]` as clockwise about `+Z` (`-1.0`) and `[0, 0, 1]` or unstated as `+Z` (`+1.0`).
- Add `AxisLimits::c_z_sense`, `AxisLimits::c_program_travel`, `Machine::c_axis`, and `Machine::reversed_c_rotary` in `crates/post/src/machine/direction.rs`.
- Refuse non-finite, zero, or non-Z C vectors (`d[2]^2 < 0.998 * |d|^2`) by name across `AxisLimits::c_z_sense`, `operation::rotary_gate::stamp_c_about`, `machine::judge::c_letter_problem`, and `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`liveStart`).
- Flip asymmetric `-Z` C travel `[lo, hi]` to `[-hi, -lo]` in `stamp_c_about`, check `sign * c` in `c_letter_problem`, and negate posted `C` (`liveCSense * Number(p.C)`) in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`liveMove`).
- Emit `  C rotary turns clockwise about +Z (-Z axis) - posted C is negated for this machine` under `MACHINE AXES` in `crates/app/src/setup_sheet/sections.rs` (`render_machine_axes`).
- Subdivide `Move.arc` moves in `crates/cl/src/cl/rotary.rs` (`stamp_c`) via `Move::segments3(tol * 0.5)`, refine chords at `tol * 0.5`, emit `arc: None`, rotate piece poses with `pose_at`, and refuse non-finite arc centers by name.
- Add end-to-end World tests in `crates/app/tests/c_axis_live_world.rs` and record the design choices in `docs/decisions/33-c-sense-and-arcs.md`.

## Cause

title: fix(sim): credit bounded 3D edge-break volumes
body:
## What changed

Stock verification now credits framed 3D edge-break volumes.
The records describe flat bisector chamfers, concave ball arcs, and convex rounded profiles.
Each segment carries an orthonormal outward bisector frame.
The verifier credits only declared material connected to the model surface.
Cuts outside the cap or below its profile still convict as gouges.

The existing #529 operation-width bound still applies.
Framed depth cannot exceed framed width.
Invalid dimensions, frames, and profiles drop the record with a diagnostic.
Project loading preserves valid profiles and full-precision framed endpoints.
Tilted work frames rotate the cap directions with the edge.
Existing Chamfer2D and v1 Deburr records retain their cone law and wire shape.
Framed records require a zero slope so older readers discard them safely.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1891-edge-break-volumes.md`.
The branch starts at upstream/main `a277dd9d51e7b4488403b946d0a3234b71ba7504`.

## Cause

EdgeBreak described only a vertical cone.
Simulation measured its reach in XY.
That model cannot describe vertical or oblique bisector caps or circular break profiles.

## Tests

The initial runtime pin `a_framed_break_survives_the_project_record_reader` failed on unchanged upstream code.
The reader loaded zero records instead of one.
The pin passes with this change.

The additional runtime pin `tiny_circle_direction_rates_do_not_underflow_into_extra_credit` caught an underflow in the first implementation.
Normalizing the circle calculation fixes it.
Restoring the old calculation reproduces the failure.

All 21 new pins pass.
All 8 legacy edge-break pins pass.

- CL `edge_volume` has 9 pins for finite caps, circle profiles, vertical and oblique edges, tiny rates, connected intervals, corrupt frames, rotation, and legacy cones.
- Sim `edge_volume_credit` has 4 pins for valid profiles and multiple passes, vertical and oblique credit, real gouges, detached caps, malformed records, and mismatched lattices.
- App `edge_volume_bound` has 2 pins for operation width/kind bounds and corrupt-frame/excess-depth refusal.
- App `project::break_dto::volume_tests` has 5 pins for loading, legacy bytes, profiles, malformed extensions, and precise endpoints.
- App `a_framed_cap_verifies_after_loading_but_a_deeper_or_forged_cut_convicts` checks real stock verification, project save/load, deeper cuts, inflated depth, and jointly forged width/depth.

All 26 mutations produced runtime failures and passed after restoration.
Old upstream sanity, simulation credit, and project-reader implementations were restored for the baseline checks.
The project-reader baseline retained only the new field plumbing needed to compile.

- framed-slope-zero; legacy-width-finite; framed-depth-bound; segment-frame-count: red, restored green.
- radius-finite; radius-half-width; radius-sag-depth; finite-span-size: red, restored green.
- unit-outward; unit-across; frame-normal-orthogonal; outward-tangent-orthogonal; across-tangent-orthogonal: red, restored green.
- connected-only; longitudinal-end-planes; cross-width-planes; inward-depth-planes: red, restored green.
- concave-circle-profile; convex-circle-profile; analytic-circle-crossings; stable-circle-sag: red, restored green.
- tilted-frame-rotation; upstream-sanity-method; upstream-sim-credit; upstream-project-reader; normalized-circle-rates: red, restored green.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 10 stages with zero failures.
The shared CL change triggered the existing batch fallback.
The gate took 41.3 minutes, including first-build compilation and existing slow fixtures.
No retry was needed.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` also passed.
Effort: max, with no escalation.

## Goldens moved

None.
`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

Release-only heavy tests and pixel snapshots did not run.
No physical machine run was performed.
New 3D toolpath generators remain in the surrounding #1827 work.
This change adds the records and simulation support they consume.

## Overlaps

No open PR changed the edge-break functions during the overlap check.
PRs #2077 and #2092 touch `project/file.rs` in other project-format areas.
This change uses `project/break_dto.rs` and leaves `project/file.rs` untouched.
No stack is required.

Changelog: Stock verification credits bounded framed 3D chamfer, ball, and rounded edge-break volumes while retaining operation bounds and real-gouge verdicts.

Fixes #1891

- Added ASCII DXF annotation (`TEXT`/`MTEXT`) reading and an original ASCII DXF writer in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/`.

- Supported revolved spun half-profiles (`CENTRELINE`/`AXIS` around `+Z`, convertible with `#743` `SpunProfile`) and extruded closed 2D contours along `X`/`Y`/`Z` with positive depth.

Turning chucks, jaws, collets, vises, parallels, and step blocks lacked parametric 2D profile authoring, DXF import/export, and post-placement profile editing. Vendor STEP fixtures needed to keep their raw STEP geometry intact rather than being replaced by approximated profiles.

title: feat(tools): convert STEP bodies to DXF half-profiles and import/export DXF
body:
## What changed

- Added a clean-room ASCII DXF writer in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/writer.rs` (`dxf::write`, `dxf::write_bytes`, `Unit::code`) emitting `HEADER` (`$INSUNITS`), `TABLES` (`LAYER`), and `ENTITIES` (`LINE`, `ARC`, `CIRCLE`).
- Added conservative stepped-band reduction in `crates/tools/src/spun_envelope.rs` (`SpunProfile::conservative_from_bands`) merging adjacent `HolderBand`s strictly upward (`max(r)`) down to at most 31 bands (`<= 64` points) and `MIN_SEGMENT`.
- Added STEP and `ToolBody` <-> ASCII DXF half-profile conversion and DXF import in `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf.rs` and `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf_import.rs` with explicit `CENTRELINE` and `PROFILE` layers.
- Added undoable `SetToolBody` constructors (`from_dxf_bytes`, `from_dxf`, `from_step_profile`, `from_placed_profile`, `profile_dxf`) in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body_dxf.rs` over `tool_body::build_spun`.
- Registered MCP tools `import_tool_holder_dxf`, `export_tool_holder_dxf`, and `convert_tool_step_to_profile` in `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_dxf_tools.rs`.
- Added conservative-envelope and half-profile-only notices, `Import DXF…`, `Export DXF…`, `Import STEP…`, and Body tab `Convert to profile` in `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs`, `tool_profile_page.rs`, and `tool_body_page.rs`.
- Recorded architectural trade-offs in `docs/decisions/743-step-dxf-half-profile.md`.

## Cause

- Direct conversion from `HolderProfile::envelope` to `SpunProfile` failed above 31 stepped bands because `2 * 32 + 2 = 66` exceeds `MAX_POINTS` (`64`).
- CamCraft lacked an ASCII DXF writer and could not export or re-import tool holder half-profiles with an explicit centreline or enforce ISO 13399 CSYS alignment on STEP-to-profile conversion.

## Tests

- Pins:

title: fix(ui): disable X/Y WCS tilt on milling setups and point to Part alignment
body:
Stacked on #1684 (merge #1684 first)

## What changed

- Added Option 1 (Slice 1) milling guard in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`.
- On `Kind::Mill` setups (`machine::kind_of(&state.world) == Kind::Mill`), `origin_fields` disables the `Tilt about X (roll)` and `Tilt about Y (pitch)` spinbuttons and shows a hint pointing to `Part alignment` on the Setup page.
- `quarter_turns` renders the 3x2 turn buttons via `turn_row`, disabling `Turn X+`, `Turn X-`, `Turn Y+`, and `Turn Y-` on milling setups with the same hover hint.
- `X origin`, `Y origin`, `Z origin`, `Turn about Z (yaw)`, `Turn Z+`, `Turn Z-`, `Level`, and `Set Origin` stay live on milling setups.
- When an existing milling WCS is already tilted (`setup_wcs_tilt::setup_problem`), `wcs_page` warns that generation will refuse it and instructs the user to click `Level` and use `Part alignment`.
- Non-mill machines (such as `Kind::Lathe`) keep X/Y tilt spinbuttons and all six quarter-turn buttons live.
- Recorded the Option 1 choice and deferred items in `docs/decisions/1542-milling-wcs-tilt-guard.md`.

## Cause

Milling generation refuses any WCS tilted off machine Z (`setup_wcs_tilt`), while the WCS page still invited users to tilt milling WCS axes via `Tilt about X (roll)`, `Tilt about Y (pitch)`, and X/Y quarter turns instead of using `Part alignment`.

## Tests

- Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page_tests.rs`:

None.

title: feat(tools)!: a tool's library holder is a reference to the entry
body:
Stacked on #2054 (branch `mkinney:issue/2018-weldon-per-taper`, with `main` merged in for #2029). Merge #2054 first; this diff then shows only the #2016 commits. Fork synced from upstream `main` at c86d6db35.

## What changed

A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a reference to the entry, not a drawn copy of its outline.

- `camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (new, `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs`), carried on `ToolBody::library`.
- `tool_body::build_library` is the one place a reference becomes a shape. `SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool` (stated and machine-default holder), the project loader and the `.camtools` reader call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before. The #828 floor for a machine-default holder is unchanged.
- Files: the tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true` when assumed) is written in place of `body`. Project v62 (the unreleased step the issue names); a `.camtools` file says version 2 when a tool names a library holder.
- Migration: an older file is not rewritten. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a custom drawn profile with the same outline, and a `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder stays the tool's own numbers.
- Refusals by tool name: an entry the library does not hold, a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon"), lengths the entry cannot take, a holder that reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, `holder` beside `body`. No other holder is put in its place.
- MCP: `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference; the reply and `get_job` show it as `holder.library`. `add_tool` refuses a `holder` reference inside `definition`; `edit_tool` refuses a `holder` patch. Skill rows updated.
- UI: with a referenced holder the tool settings show the holder diameter and length the laws read as text, not as two fields. The Profile tab names the entry and the picker shows it. The unchanged outline applied again keeps the reference; one edited point makes the holder a custom profile (one undo step).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2016-holder-reference.md`.

## How tested

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on the final head (tools, app and ui suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. macOS (m5).

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/holder_reference.rs`
  - `every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy`: for every library entry, at the default and at other lengths, picked and assumed: the judged tool, envelope, band stack, stamp term and facets equal those of the drawn copy an older build stored, also after a save and load.
  - `an_older_project_loads_as_custom_holders_with_the_same_collision_result`: a v61 project with a drawn copy and a plain holder cylinder loads with the same reads, operation status and warnings (the BT30 flange strikes the fixture wall, hit for hit).
  - `an_older_tool_library_loads_as_custom_holders_and_a_new_one_round_trips_the_reference`
  - `an_unknown_entry_refuses_the_file_by_name_and_never_lands_another_holder` (project and `.camtools`)
  - `a_library_holder_is_the_reference_in_the_document_and_the_file`
  - `the_unchanged_outline_keeps_the_reference_and_an_edited_point_makes_it_custom`
  - `mcp_set_tool_holder_writes_the_reference`
- `crates/tools/src/holder_library_ref.rs` unit tests.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_holder_reference.rs`: `a_library_holder_sizes_the_holder_fields_until_its_outline_is_edited`, `the_profile_tab_names_the_entry_and_the_picker_shows_it`.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux. The release tier and the pixel-snapshot lanes (no snapshot PNG changed).
- No real v0.21.0 file was read: the older file in the tests is this build's file rewritten to the older form (`body` with the drawn copy, version 61 / 1).
- The app was not driven by hand.

## Notes for the reviewer

- A build of main between #1453 and this change reads v62 and would drop the `holder` key (development builds only; v0.21.0 refuses v62).
- A corrected library entry now reaches every project that names it. A copy kept the old numbers.
- The tool record's `holder_d`/`holder_len` are not overwritten by the entry (they are what the tool goes back to when the holder is cleared, and writing them would move the stamp). The settings show the entry's numbers.

Changelog: A tool's library holder is stored as a reference to the library entry (name, gauge length, projection) in the project and tool library files, not as a drawn copy; the tool settings show the entry's holder size. Breaking: v0.21.0 and older refuse a file that names a library holder.

Effort: max (no escalation)

BREAKING CHANGE: a project or tool library saved with a library holder states it as a reference (project v62, `.camtools` version 2); v0.21.0 and older refuse such a file.

Process change: yes

Fixes #2016

title: fix(ui): read status strip, ribbon tabs, window margin and drop hint from theme
body:
Stacked on #2027 (merge #2027 first)

## What changed

- Added five geometry tokens to `theme::Tokens` (`window_margin`, `status_h`, `ribbon_tab_pad_x`, `ribbon_tab_gap`, `ribbon_tab_stroke`) and `clamp::RADIUS_WINDOW` (`24`).
- Updated `Tokens::DARK` and `Tokens::LIGHT` in `theme/tables.rs` with defaults that preserve existing dark and light pixel geometry (`6.0`, `22.0`, `12.0`, `2.0`, `2.0`).
- Added `theme::status_h(t)` to return the maximum of `t.status_h`, `t.control_height + 4.0`, and `t.font_row * 1.3 + 4.0`.
- Wired `Tokens::style()` to read `spacing.window_margin` from `self.window_margin` instead of `item_spacing_y.max(6.0)`.
- Wired `shell::shell_layout` to size the bottom status bar with `theme::status_h(&pal)`.
- Wired `panes::ribbon_tabs` to read left inset from `pal.item_spacing_x`, tab padding from `pal.ribbon_tab_pad_x`, inter-tab gap from `pal.ribbon_tab_gap`, and underline stroke from `pal.ribbon_tab_stroke`.
- Wired `file_drop::paint_hint` to read border inset from `pal.window_margin`, corner radius from `pal.radius_window`, and stroke thickness and text size from `pal.font_label`.
- Split `theme_files::names` into `crates/ui/src/egui_app/theme_files/names.rs` to keep every file under 400 lines.
- Added `docs/decisions/2064-theme-shell-metrics.md`.

## Cause

Shell metrics for window margin, bottom status height, ribbon tab spacing and stroke, and the file drop hint used hardcoded constants or `item_spacing_y` instead of dedicated theme tokens.

## Tests

All five pinning tests failed before the fix on unchanged `base-2027` and pass after the final edit:

- `theme_shell_metrics::window_margin_comes_from_own_token_not_item_spacing`
- `theme_shell_metrics::status_h_and_ribbon_tab_keys_parse_and_clamp`
- `egui_app::tests::ribbon_rows::issue_2064_pins::status_strip_height_tracks_theme_controls_and_status_h`
- `egui_app::tests::ribbon_rows::issue_2064_pins::ribbon_tabs_follow_theme_spacing_pad_gap_and_stroke`
- `egui_app::tests::file_drop::issue_2064_pins::drop_hint_reads_window_margin_radius_and_font_from_theme`

Mutation checks (each reverted or loosened code path failed red, then passed green after restoring):

1. `theme.rs` `Tokens::style()` `window_margin` reverted to `item_spacing_y.max(6.0)` -> `window_margin_comes_from_own_token_not_item_spacing` failed, restored passed.
2. `theme_files/overlay.rs` clamps on the 5 new keys loosened -> `status_h_and_ribbon_tab_keys_parse_and_clamp` failed, restored passed.
3. `theme.rs` `status_h()` stripped to `t.status_h` -> `status_strip_height_tracks_theme_controls_and_status_h` failed, restored passed.
4. `shell.rs` `.exact_size(22.0)`, `panes.rs` `ribbon_tabs` literals, and `file_drop.rs` `paint_hint` literals reverted -> all 3 `issue_2064_pins` tests failed, restored passed.

Gate and lint after final edit:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed (`ui lib` 832 passed / 6 ignored, `boundary` 3, `boundary_picks` 6, `sinker_setup` 2, `theme_files` 14, `theme_shell_metrics` 2, `waterjet_tool` 1; 0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed with zero warnings.

## Goldens moved

None (`0` `.nc`, `.cl`, or `.png` files changed).

## Not exercised

- `assets/themes/theme.json.example` was not updated here because #2038 creates that file on top of #2027 and this branch stacks one level on #2027.
- Unchanged non-UI workspace crates and Windows-made pixel snapshot goldens did not run in the quick gate.

## Overlaps

- `#2027` (stacked on it; merge `#2027` first): modifies `theme.rs` (`Tokens`, `clamp`, `geom_legal`), `theme/tables.rs`, `theme_files.rs` (`names`, `COLOR_NAMES`, `GEOM_NAMES`), `theme_files/overlay.rs` (`apply_overlay`), `shell.rs` (constants above `STATUS_H`), `panes.rs` (`ribbon_tabs`), and `tests/ribbon_rows.rs`.
- `#2029`, `#2023`, `#1798`, `#1330` touch other functions in `shell.rs`; `#1798` touches other functions in `panes.rs`. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Read status strip height, ribbon tab metrics, window margin, and drop hint geometry from theme tokens
Fixes #2064

## Review screenshots

These screenshots show the actual shell, tool editor, and file drop hint.
The renderer uses `egui_kittest` and the actual `View3D` GPU output at 1440 × 960 pixels.
The ribbon and status images are crops of that output.

Both runs use the same dark theme and scene.
The theme sets `window_margin=20`, `status_h=48`, `ribbon_tab_pad_x=24`, `ribbon_tab_gap=12`, and `ribbon_tab_stroke=6`.
It also sets `item_spacing_x=16`, `radius_window=20`, and `font_label=15`.
These values make the changed behavior visible. The default values preserve the previous geometry.

The after run uses the consumers at `bacb784b0207c43ea610bb8da9c8beb15f9ba61b`.
For the before run, the temporary harness restores the parent ribbon tab function, status height, window margin expression, and drop hint body.
The before run keeps the new token schema to load the same theme file.
It keeps an unused palette argument on the drop hint function so the harness compiles.
Thus, the before run shows the parent consumer behavior with the same theme configuration.
It does not use an unchanged parent checkout.

The eight PNG files exist only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.
No screenshot, capture harness, log, or review evidence was added to this PR branch.

title: fix(import): stop a STEP pass after a few runaway faces
body:
## What changed

- All face meters and edge-curve meters of one shell pass share one pass budget (`Pass`, new `step_meter.rs`).
- Each meter counts its first refusal in the pass one time. A refusal is a cap that ran out, a division that did not converge, or a boundary-search fault.
- At `PASS_TRIPS` (3) trips the pass stops. Then each meter answers its fixed point, and each face in flight ends within one sweep.
- The stopped pass is refused by name. The refusal names the first face or edge that really tripped. It adds: "the tessellation stopped after 3 faces or edges ran out of evaluations; more of the model may be broken".
- A stopped pass is never "continuous". Thus no coarser mesh is kept for it.
- A meter that the stop cut short is not a trip. Its `exhaust` and its search faults are not recorded. Thus a refusal never names a healthy face.
- `Meter` moved from `step_guard.rs` to `step_meter.rs`. This keeps `step_guard.rs` under 400 lines (now 365).

## Cause

The 150 M evaluation cap applied to each face, not to the pass. Each runaway face spent a full cap (10-15 s) before it tripped. A file with N runaway faces thus cost N caps divided by the core count.

## Tests

Pins (red before the fix: yes):

- `step_meter::tests::a_pass_with_many_runaway_faces_stops_after_a_few_trips`. A shell with 31 runaway faces. Before: `31 runaway faces spent 6200175 evaluations, bound 2200011`. After: under the bound (3 caps plus one cap for each worker thread).
- `import_step_guard::a_shell_of_many_runaway_faces_is_refused_after_a_few_trips`. End to end: `bspline_discontinuous.step` with face #53 listed 40 more times. It is refused by name, and the refusal says that the pass stopped.
- `step_meter::tests::the_pass_stops_at_the_trip_limit_and_a_stopped_meter_is_not_a_trip`
- `step_meter::tests::a_stopped_pass_of_proven_faces_is_not_continuous`
- `step_meter::tests::edge_trips_count_against_the_pass_budget`
- `step_meter::tests::the_refusal_of_a_stopped_pass_says_it_stopped`
- `step_meter::tests::a_pass_with_one_runaway_face_is_not_stopped` (unchanged behaviour below the limit)

Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pins were run, and the code was restored:

- `spend` ignores a stopped pass: red.
- `spend_many` ignores a stopped pass: red.
- A stopped pass can be continuous: red.
- `exhaust` on a stopped pass: red.
- `flag` on a stopped pass: red.
- Faces do not share the pass (the old code): red (4 pins).
- Edges do not share the pass: red.
- The refusal has no stop note: red.

title: feat(turning): lathe chucks fit to the stock in the dialog, inside grip, stepped jaws
body:
First slice of #1468. Fork synced from `upstream/main` at 31f8d03d7 (branch cut from it, not from a tag). Not stacked: no open PR changes these files except the camcraft-mcp skill (#1738, #1817, #2037 edit other rows).

## What changed

- **Dialog: "Fit to the stock" for a lathe chuck.** "Add accessory…" shows a **Fit to the stock** checkbox for the 3-jaw, 4-jaw and collet chuck. Ticked, Place queues `InsertAccessory` with the existing `OnStock` placement; the grip diameter (or collet bore) is shown as "(set by the fit)" and disabled, and the pose rows give way to a line that says what the fit does. The box opens ticked when the setup's stock reads as round.
- **Inside grip** (`JawChuck::grip`, `outside` | `inside`). An inside jaw runs inward from the grip diameter; its gripping face is the arc of the bore it opens into, drawn circumscribed (flats on the grip circle, steps of at most 1/256 turn), so the drawn steel is never less than the jaw.
- **Stepped jaws** (`step_height`, `step_depth`; both 0 for plain jaws). Below the step height the jaw reaches the step depth past the gripping face, under the work. A stock fit seats the stock on the step: the chuck's face goes the step height below the stock's underside.
- **Refusals by name** (all in `camcraft_sim::chuck::jaw::check`): a step figure that is not finite, negative or over 5000 mm; one step figure without the other; a step as tall as its jaw; a step or an inside jaw that reaches the axis; steps or inside jaws that would meet each other; an inside jaw wider than its bore, shorter than its own arc, or past the body. A stock fit with an inside grip is refused ("an inside grip opens into the work's bore, which the stock's box does not give"); the dialog unticks and disables the box for an inside grip and says why.
- **MCP:** `add_accessory` and `set_accessory` take `grip`; the `dimensions` object takes `step_height` and `step_depth`; the result's `accessory` shows `grip` for a jaw chuck. The camcraft-mcp skill row now lists the three chuck kinds, `fit_to_stock`, `grip` and the step figures.
- **Files:** the three new fields are `serde(default)`, so a project saved before this reads as plain outside jaws, and the default chuck's mesh is unchanged to the triangle (pinned).
- Guide: `site/content/guide/set-up/workholding.md` describes the chuck rows. Decision record: `docs/decisions/1468-chuck-options.md`.

The jaw geometry lives in `crates/sim/src/chuck/jaw.rs` (new, with its provenance line); `chuck.rs` keeps the body, the collet and the round-stock read. No new crate dependency.

## Collision consequences (safety floor)

A generated chuck is an ordinary meshed fixture, so the new jaws reach the lathe holder law and the post gate through the same path as #1442:

- `inside_grip_jaws_are_steel_that_blocks_the_post`: a holder whose leg rides through inside-grip jaws is named and the post is blocked; the same holder 2 mm over the jaws posts.
- `stepped_jaws_are_steel_where_they_stand_under_the_work`: the same for stepped jaws with the face lowered by the step height.

title: feat(tools)!: cutting data by work material - Unknown default row, stepdown/stepover, stock material
body:
## What changed

Tool cutting data by work material (#2015, part of #2007):

- **`Unknown` row.** Every tool's cutting data now holds an `Unknown` row (file word `unknown`; in code `CuttingRow::material == None`). It is what the tool runs when no row names the material in force, and the fallback for a row's missing stepdown/stepover. It is derived from the tool's own rpm/feed and stored only when it states something more (other numbers, or a step) - so a new tool has it, every older tool reads its own numbers as it, and plain tools are stored, saved and shown to MCP byte for byte as before. A command that moves the running numbers away from a derived row stores it first. A waterjet (recipes) and an electrode (rpm 0) get none, so a sane tool never turns insane.
- **Stepdown and stepover per row** (mm, optional). They seed an operation's stepdown/stepover only inside an undoable command (quick-add, MCP `add_operation`, the feature recognizer, `SetWorkMaterial`, `SetStockMaterial`, retargeting a tool), never on load. Seeded kinds: pocket, adaptive, offset, slot, 3-D pocket, multi-axis rough, face (stepover; stepdown only when staged), 2-D contour (stepdown). A stepover wider than the cutter is refused by tool name.
- **Setup stock material.** New `StockMaterial` component on a setup's stock and the undoable `SetStockMaterial` command (MCP `set_stock_material`, stock page "Material" group). The row is picked by the stock's material, then the document's, then `Unknown`. The tools' running rpm/feed (the posted S word) follow the document material only - a tool is shared by every setup.
- **`.camtools`/project migration.** `PROJECT_VERSION` 62 -> 63 (the issue's "61 to 62" predates #1453's bump). A v62 project loads with each tool's own rpm/feed as its `Unknown` row; nothing it runs moves. `.camtools` reader accepts versions 1, 2 and 3; the writer writes 3 only when a library holds a stated `Unknown` row or a step (otherwise 1, or 2 for left-hand taps, as before). An `Unknown` row that only repeats the tool's own rpm/feed is not written, so plain tools save byte for byte as before (MCP `get_job` output unchanged for them).
- **Tool page.** The "Cutting data by material" group is now a table: Material, Spindle rpm, Feed, Stepdown, Stepover (0 = not stated). The `Unknown` row is first, its material fixed, not removable.
- **Behaviour change, inside a command only:** stating a document material the tool has no row for now runs the tool's `Unknown` row (before: the previous material's numbers stayed). An operation's milling feed still moves only for a row that names the material (#890's rule), so picking a material never overwrites hand-set op feeds.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2015-unknown-cutting-row.md` (why `Option<WorkMaterial>` and not a `WorkMaterial::Unknown` variant: `WorkMaterial::row()` indexes the handbook table).

Base: upstream/main (`31f8d03d7`); no file overlap with #2029 (it does not touch `tool_cutting_rows.rs`; both touch `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in different places). Fork synced at the current upstream main for this branch.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/tools/tests/unknown_row.rs` (6): selection order, step fallback, derivation once and only from the running numbers, kinds that get none, refusals (bad steps, `Unknown` twice).
- `crates/app/tests/cutting_unknown_row.rs` (9): `a_new_tool_gets_its_unknown_row_from_its_own_numbers`, `a_v62_project_loads_its_tool_numbers_as_the_unknown_row_with_no_loss`, `a_v1_tool_library_loads_with_the_unknown_row_and_steps_write_v3`, `the_row_is_picked_by_the_stock_then_the_document_then_unknown`, `a_second_setup_stock_material_seeds_only_its_own_operations`, `steps_seed_only_in_commands_and_the_stock_material_round_trips`, `a_project_with_no_new_rows_posts_the_same_s_and_f_words` (posts, re-saves as v62, reloads, re-posts: identical S/F words), `a_stated_stepover_wider_than_the_cutter_is_refused_by_tool_name`, `mcp_sets_the_stock_material_as_one_undo_step`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/stock_material.rs`: the stock page's Material group sits between Shape and Size, and a pick is one undoable `SetStockMaterial`.
- Updated to the new law: `crates/app/tests/tool_cutting_rows.rs` (stating plastics, which has no row, now runs the tool's Unknown row), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutting_rows.rs` unit tests (Unknown is shown, never added).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (macOS, m5): green on 75031d5f9 (tools, app and ui suites; 6.2 min). Clippy on camcraft-tools, camcraft-app, camcraft-ui: clean (`--all-targets -D warnings`).

- The camcraft-mcp skill row for `set_stock_material` is a follow-up (process-file change): #2076.
- A per-setup spindle speed (the S word by stock material) is out of scope: the tool's running rpm follows the document material.

title: fix(xtask): share one job budget across the lanes of a gate wave
body:
## What changed

- New `xtask/src/budget.rs`: one job budget for each gate run. The default is 6 (`budget::DEFAULT`). `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=<n>` (1 or more) overrides it. A bad value prints a note and keeps 6.
- `exec.rs` sets `-j` and `--test-threads=` of each step when it runs the step (`budget::scale`):
  - A wave of N lanes gives each lane `budget / N` jobs, minimum 1.
  - A step that runs alone gets the full budget. This applies to each quick, batch and test step, and to each release step that runs alone.
  - A value that a step sets on purpose (not the plan default `6`) can only go down.
- `lanes::waves(steps, limit)` takes the lane limit. The release tier gives `budget::lane_limit` = `budget / 2`, minimum 1. `LIMIT = 4` is removed. A budget of 6 gives 3 lanes of 2 jobs.
- The gate prints the budget line at the start, and `-- wave K: N lane(s) x -j M` before each wave. `--dry-run` prints the same lines.
- The `gate` and `runners` skills have the rule: the sum of `-j` of all builds on one machine stays at or below its core count.
- `docs/decisions/2057-gate-job-budget.md` records the choices.

## Overlap with #1952 (#1941)

The plan builders (`plan.rs`, `quick.rs`, `single.rs`) do not change. The executor rewrites the flags at run time. Thus each step that #1952 adds also gets the budget. `git merge-tree` of this branch with the head of #1952 is clean, so this PR does not stack on it. After the two PRs merge, one line of `docs/decisions/1941-gate-step-per-binary.md` ("four at most") is old. The cut can correct it when it collects the decisions.

## Readings

`cargo xtask gate release --dry-run` (start):

```

[01] debug build (--no-run)
...
-- wave 3: 3 lane(s) x -j 2
```

- `scale_keeps_deliberate_values_low_and_child_args_alone`
- `the_override_must_be_a_whole_number_of_one_or_more`

The `lanes_tests.rs` tests now give the limit 4 explicitly. The executor test sets the budget to 6, so that its two lanes overlap with each value of `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS`.

Added modal `C` holding inside `pole_sin_tol` near `A = 0` and weighted angular step minimization across branches for smooth zero crossings.
Added continuous `C` unwrapping inside sections, safe-retract re-wrapping, named refusals for invalid geometry or travel overflow, and quarter-point chord subdivision in `solve_path` and `solve_toolpath`.
Exported `kinematics` in `crates/post/src/lib.rs`, added tests in `crates/post/tests/ac_trunnion_ik.rs` and `crates/post/src/kinematics/tests.rs`, and recorded the design decision in `docs/decisions/1965-ac-trunnion-ik.md`.

## Cause
The codebase lacked a shared pure-Rust XYZAC table-table inverse kinematics solver in `camcraft-post`, so machine checking and post processors had no common kinematic core for off-pivot offsets, rotary branch selection, pole holding, continuous C unwrapping, and chord subdivision.

## Tests
- Pins (`cargo test -p camcraft-post --test ac_trunnion_ik`): 7 passed (`round_trip_fk_ik_with_nonzero_offsets_within_micron`, `asymmetric_a_limits_select_reachable_branch_and_refuse_unreachable`, `pole_near_zero_holds_previous_modal_c_instead_of_snapping_to_zero`, `smooth_crossing_of_a_zero_without_180_deg_c_flip`, `continuous_c_unwrapping_and_safe_retract_rewrapping`, `subdivides_linear_moves_beyond_chord_tolerance_for_tip_accuracy`, `refuses_malformed_machine_geometry_and_non_finite_inputs`).
- Unit tests (`cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib kinematics`): 4 passed (`rollover_wraps_into_0_to_360_at_initial_and_safe_retract`, `positive_only_a_limits_reorient_c_at_pole_within_chord_tolerance`, `solve_toolpath_converts_cl_moves_and_detects_retract`, `refuses_non_positive_path_options_and_parallel_spindle`).
- Full crate suite (`cargo test -p camcraft-post`): all lib unit and integration suites passed before the final `solve.rs`/`travel.rs` extraction, and `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` plus `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final tree.
- Mutation checks on `ac_trunnion_ik`:
  - Removed `pub mod kinematics;` in `crates/post/src/lib.rs`: failed compile -> restored -> passed.
  - Replaced modal `C` hold at pole with `0.0` in `solve.rs`: `pole_near_zero_holds_previous_modal_c_instead_of_snapping_to_zero` and `smooth_crossing_of_a_zero_without_180_deg_c_flip` failed -> restored -> passed.
  - Disabled weighted minimum-cost branch selection in `solve.rs`: `smooth_crossing_of_a_zero_without_180_deg_c_flip` failed (`dC=180`) -> restored -> passed.
  - Replaced strict `unwrap_near` + `C.travel` refusal in `Continuous` mode with re-wrap turn search in `solve.rs`: `continuous_c_unwrapping_and_safe_retract_rewrapping` failed -> restored -> passed.
  - Disabled `exceeds_chord_tol` check in `path.rs`: `subdivides_linear_moves_beyond_chord_tolerance_for_tip_accuracy` failed (`got 1` segment) -> restored -> passed.

## Goldens moved

## Not exercised
Wiring `.mch` trunnion schema fields (#1962), `mach4.cps` posting (#1968), `G93` inverse-time feeds (#1966), and `machine::check_ops` integration (#1969) remain out of scope for those downstream issues.

title: feat(motion): cut the adaptive stock ring from the air (issue 1950, rounds A-B)
body:
﻿Draft. Rounds A to E of issue #1950 (a default whole-model Adaptive 3D Pocket exceeds the planner budgets on the stock ring). This PR does not close the issue: the D plate level still goes to the Offset rings, now by the hop budget. Round F is open.

Head: c3509172c331eedacbf61f8a07855cadd12fdb75

## What changed

Round A (motion crate):
- New planner `plan_from_air` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs`. It cuts the stock ring from the air side inward. Sources: Held 1991 (LNCS 500), Held and Spielberger 2009 (CAD 41(7)), Stori and Wright 2000.
- `Raster::open_air` marks the air band as open. The walk functions of `raster.rs` moved to `raster/walk.rs` with no change of logic.

Round B (plumbing, no new algorithm):
- `machining3d::open_sides` takes a `stock_band` argument. `machining3d::stock_band(r, adaptive)` gives `2r + OPEN_SLACK` for Adaptive and `r - OPEN_SLACK` for each other strategy.
- New entry `machining3d::pocket3d_open_prev(facets, footprint, stock, p, mask)`. The stock goes through `ladder`, `hsm::plan_level`, `adaptive_passes` and `hsm_passes`.
- A plan from the air whose worst reading is over the load bound is refused by name. The level then goes to the Offset rings with a note.

Round C:
- App arm (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, `open_side.rs`): a whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy (not shell, not rest roughing) uses the wide band and calls `pocket3d_open_prev` with the setup stock outline. Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and each other strategy keep the old band.
- Microlift joins (`adaptive/air_links.rs`): each pass is joined to the one before it by the existing `LinkLaw`. Each join is walked again on the stock. A pass with no proved join keeps its retract hop. Source: Otkur and Lazoglu 2007.

Round D:
- Air entry: `machining2d::in_air(stock, e, r)`. Where the first pass of an air plan starts 0.005 mm clear of the stock outline, the ladder enters the level by an axial plunge there. A tool that is not centre-cutting keeps the old entry law.
- Fixture refusal: `air_band_refusal` refuses the Adaptive whole-model op at generation when a tagged fixture meets the air band. The message starts with `AIR_BAND_FIXTURE` and names the fixture. The post gate is not changed.

Round E:
- Cause of the round D crossing at (-8.12, -35.61). A probe printed the crossing pairs of the air passes before and after the joins. Before the joins: 40 pairs. After the joins: the same 40 pairs. So the joins and the air entry did not cause it. Pass 0 is the spiral (3 closed fronts and a closing lap on ring 3 at y -35.607). Passes 1-21 are open-front runs. Passes 22-45 are wall laps. The pairs were:
  - the spiral and the first open runs: a lead-in starts one load width back, on the ring 3 lap, and steps past it;
  - each open run and the run of the next front (1-4, 4-7, ...);
  - open runs and wall laps (4-37, 7-22, ...): a run that meets the part wall cuts across the laps.
- Fix, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_uncross.rs` (new): each new pass drops the chords that cross a kept pass, by the plan's own law (`guard::crosses`). The pass then continues as a new piece. Each piece is read on the stock as before, so the rest and the load readings stay true. Result: 0 crossing pairs before the joins.
- The joins: with the bare passes clean, `LinkLaw::late` (a lead whose graze joins the pass) put crossings back, because the lead runs back across an earlier pass. `air_joins` now keeps a late join only when the grown pass crosses no other pass. If it crosses, the join falls back to the retract hop. Result: 0 crossing pairs after the joins.
- The crossing check, the load check, the verify gate and the budgets are not changed.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs` (427 lines) is split. The landing spots (wall margin, spots along the first pass, the helix placement, the plunge spot) move to `machining3d/descent_place.rs` (120 lines) with no change of logic. `descent.rs` is now 327 lines.

## Readings, round E (D plate, R = 5, 70 x 70 stock, one level, debug)

| Reading | Round C/D (crossing plan) | Round E |
|---|---|---|
| Crossing through `adaptive_passes` | at (-8.12, -35.61) | none |
| Passes | 47 | 61 |
| Retract hops (budget 8) | 3 | 23 |
| Worst load (of D) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) |
| Slack to the bound | 0.00135 deg | 0.00135 deg |
| Moves (budget 120000) | 17614 | 17549 |
| Cut / air / lift (mm) | - / - / 107.3 | 2632 / 338 / 108 |
| Rest (limit 0.02) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| Time, one level (debug) | 21.8 s | 22.0 s |
| Strategy of the level | Offset rings (crossing) | Offset rings (hop budget) |

22 of the 23 hops are late joins that were refused because their lead crosses an earlier pass. The earlier reading of 3 hops came from joins whose leads crossed. The hop budget was not raised.

## Posted G-code

- Changed. Each whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy and a stock outline uses the wide band. A level whose air plan is clean and in its budgets is cut from the air. Other levels go to the Offset rings by name, as before.
- On the D plate, the stock ring level is still cut by the Offset rings (by name, now for the hop budget).
- Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and the non-Adaptive strategies post as before.

## Pinning tests

- `machining2d::adaptive::air_uncross::tests::a_crossing_chord_is_dropped_and_the_pass_goes_on` (new).
- `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`: still red, now on the hop budget (23 over 8). Ignored with a round F reason.
- `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`: red on its hop assert (23 over 8). Ignored with a round F reason. Its rest and move asserts hold.

- `pocket3d_air_band`: 4 pass.

Round E runs:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib -- ring_tests air_rings air_uncross machining3d pocket adaptive`: 87 pass, 0 fail, 9 ignored (built before the descent split; the split is a move only, and clippy built it clean).
- App: `level_links` 25, `open_band` 7, `operations` 120 / 6 ignored, `pocket3d_air_band` 4, `pocket3d_hsm` 1 / 2 ignored, `pocket3d_open_side` 7, `whole_model_pocket` 5 / 1 ignored. All pass (after the split).

## What changed

Show the selected tool's editable settings directly in Properties.
Use the same form from the browser and the setup's Tool list.
Keep geometry, holder/body/profile, cutting data, tool numbers and identification fields with the selected tool.
Move catalog browsing, Add/New, import/export and import options into a separate Tool library dock tab.
Open that tab from Tools or browser View > Tool library… without replacing the Properties subject.
Keep new-tool creation in its existing window.
Preserve the explicit editor's original wide layout and command paths.
Name per-tool metadata Tool information to distinguish it from library browsing.

The control split and alternatives are recorded in docs/decisions/2002-tool-properties.md.
Source inspection found no control literally named Support features and no MCP or script verb that opens the catalog by page name.
Parent head: 028a0ad0ed6711e39fc584d55be8a987906a81c5.

body:
## What changed

Each theme now gives the ribbon row heights, the gaps and the glyph ink. The shell reads them from the active table. It has no row number and no ink literal of its own.

- Both theme files set the rows 24 / 4 / 12 / 18 / 4. The caption gap is 12 (the table says 8 or larger) because `glyph_px` is 22 in both files, and the button label would touch the caption at 8.
- `teal-night` ink is white. `horizon-day` ink is `#1F242A`: its ribbon ground is near white, and white would vanish there.

title: fix(ui): lay a lathe's spindle axis across the viewport
body:
## What changed

The cause of #1993 is in the camera, not in the envelope. The envelope already is a cylinder about world Z for a lathe (`crates/post/src/machine/envelope.rs:27-60`). The turning paths also use world Z as the spindle axis. But `Camera::basis_right` (`crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`, before this PR: `normalize([fy, -fx, 0.0])`) always crossed the view with world +Z. Thus world Z could never lie across the screen, and each cylinder about Z stood vertical.

- New `crates/ui/src/view_frame.rs`: `ViewFrame { Mill, Lathe }`, a proper rotation between the orbit frame and the world. `Mill` is the identity. `Lathe`: local x = world -Z, local y = world +Y, local z = world +X.
- `Camera` gets a `frame` field. `eye` and `basis_right` map through the frame. `basis_up`, `mvp`, `ray_through`, `dolly_cursor`, the traced-stock eye and the view cube read that one basis. Draw and pick stay on one matrix.
- `Camera::toward` converts the world direction of the view cube into the frame. `Camera::pan` now uses the Z part of the right vector (it was always zero before).
- `Camera::with_frame` sets a frame and its home view. `view_frame::sync` runs at the top of `viewport_panel` in each frame. It reads `camcraft_app::machine::kind_of` (the machine of the active setup). A change of frame takes the home view of the frame. Fit and "nothing to frame" keep the frame.
- Screen rule for a lathe: the right-handed program frame (ISO 841) does not change. The home view puts world +Z (the spindle axis, away from the chuck) to the right and world +X (the cross-slide) up. World +Y then points to the viewer. The frame comes from the machine kind in the machine data, not from a hard-coded hand per machine.

Display only. The world, the WCS, the toolpaths and the posted G-code do not change: no post or generator code reads `Camera`. The frame change is view state, not a command (the test checks that the history does not change).

The decision record is `docs/decisions/1993-lathe-envelope-axis.md`.

## What #2019 still needs

This PR does the camera part. #2019 stays open for:

- The world gizmo: show Z and X only on a lathe, and Y only when the machine has a Y axis.
- A decision for mill-turn machines (this PR keeps them in the milling frame).
- View cube face names for the lathe frame, if the maintainer wants them (the cube now names world directions in each frame).
- The pin that the posted program of a turning golden does not change.

## Overlap

PR #2006 changes `crates/ui/src/work_envelope.rs`. This PR does not touch that file. PR #1689 changes `Camera::eye` and `Camera::mvp` in `crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`. This PR changes `Camera::eye` too, so a small merge conflict can occur in `eye`.

## Refresh (merge of main 17a8c6e76)

- New head: 4eb577be305761c352696384cf4426ae8f207de4 (old head c620c1255b710ce1bce0e368c542c94db255f901).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`: both sides added a test module after `mod work_envelope;`. The merge keeps the two: `mod lathe_view;` (#1993) and `mod camera_target;` (#1997).
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs` merged without a conflict. `reset_for_open` now calls `frame_all` (#1997). `frame_all` keeps the camera frame (this PR), and `view_frame::sync` keeps the target and the distance. Thus an open frames the part, and a lathe keeps its frame.
- Tests after the merge (debug, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, filters lathe_view, camera_target, view_frame, work_envelope, camera, frame, viewcube, orbit, pan): 63 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. This includes `lathe_view::*` (3 tests), `camera_target::frame_target_is_the_same_with_the_envelope_on_and_off` and `camera_target::open_frames_the_part_with_the_envelope_on_and_off`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Delta class: DELTA (one hand-resolved file, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`).

## Tests

Pinned by these tests in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/lathe_view.rs`:

- `a_lathe_lays_the_envelope_along_the_spindle_axis_left_to_right`: through the real shell, a lathe machine file gives the lathe frame and its home view. Screen right is world +Z and screen up is world +X. The envelope ends stay at the Z travel (-197, 3). The projected spindle axis is level, +Z is to the right, and the X radius goes up. The history does not change.
- `a_mill_again_takes_the_milling_view_back`: a mill machine file again gives the milling frame and the house isometric.
- `the_lathe_frame_keeps_pick_pan_and_the_view_cube_on_one_basis`: in the lathe frame, the basis is orthonormal and right-handed, the centre ray hits the target, a pan moves along the spindle axis, and the view cube and orbit keep the frame.

Existing tests run (debug, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, filters law_tests, viewcube, eye_geom, view_names, orbit, pan, iso, box_select, one_pick_rule, wcs_circle, wcs_part_point, wcs_pick_click, work_envelope, frame, edge_click, review_1710, camera, lathe_view): 144 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No visible app window was opened. The screenshots below come from an offscreen render.
- The pixel snapshots (release lane) are not run. The lathe view does not change a mill snapshot.

Changelog: The viewport shows a lathe with its spindle axis from left to right and the cross-slide up, so the work envelope lies along the spindle axis (#1993).

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1993

## Screenshots

Method: the real shell and the viewport, rendered offscreen at 1280x800 by the UI test harness. No app window was opened. The same steps run before and after: mount a lathe machine with Z travel -197 to 3, turn on "Show work envelope", then set the camera target to (0, 0, -97) and the distance to 420.

Before (origin/main, 2f6de7c5b). The envelope cylinder stands upright:

![before: lathe envelope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/1f3a51015cc13780c217388ed587a932e61ee5ea/pr-2023/lathe-before.png)

After (this PR, c620c1255). The spindle axis runs left to right. The cylinder lies along it:

![after: lathe envelope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/1f3a51015cc13780c217388ed587a932e61ee5ea/pr-2023/lathe-after.png)

body:
**Round 6 done (head `185a69f1e06bd7737a3c35c2ed1ae74c6716c112`). The goldens are regenerated and read. The full quick gate is not run (its plan is all app suites). The PR stays a draft.**

Readings (debug), round 6, each green:
- app: `golden_cl` 33, `conformance` 7, `solid_law_goldens` 7, `program_units` 7, `arc_entry` 3, `contour_start_point` 8, `control_comp` 5, `wear_comp` 5, `lathe_post` 7, `lathe_post_css` 10, `lathe_post_inch` 6, `adaptive_trochoid` 12, `microarc_test_part` 2, `thread_boss` 12, `engrave_law` 9, `mill2d_b` 9, `verify` 21, `trochoid_confine` 6, `trochoid_law` 7, `trochoid_op` 5, `top_z_stock_over` 2, `tinyg_post` 18, `tormach_post` 10, `tormach_end_units` 7, `program_comments` 4, `post_cycle_feed_spindle` 8, `plasma_post_refusals` 7, and the lathe, wire, sinker, c-axis and probe post suites; lib `ladder_planes`.

Changelog: Depth-stepping operations no longer cut a first level at Top Z when no stock stands over Top Z; posted programs have one level fewer.

Effort: high (no escalation).


## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/levels.rs`: the shared level law `cut_levels` starts at `top - stepdown` and ends at `bottom` exactly. `top 20, bottom 0, step 5` gives `[15, 10, 5, 0]`. Each level below the first is the same float as before. `cut_levels` is now `pub`.
- Round 3: `cut_levels_under(top, material_top, bottom, stepdown)`. When the material top stands over Top Z, the level at Top Z stays (the old ladder, byte for byte). `None`, or a material top at or under Top Z, gives the new ladder.
- Round 3: `camcraft_motion::approach::Approach` gets the runtime field `material_top: Option<f64>` (default `None`, not in the project file). The callers that carry `links` use `cut_levels_under`: pocket, HSM pocket, trochoidal pocket, adaptive trochoidal, slot, contour, bore, circular (not vault), 3D entry ladder.
- Round 3: `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` sets `material_top` from `stock_top_z` (in the generator frame). `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs`: `ladder_planes` reads the same material top (part top or setup stock top), so the region planes are the generator levels.
- Round 3: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_bore.rs`, `contour_step.rs`, `contour.rs`: a bore-side level transition whose column no earlier descent opened starts at the top of the cut plus the plunge height. It does not start at the floor of the level before.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs`: vault mode. A plane at Top Z is dropped. An inner ring keeps the floor of the ring before it as its first level.
- `crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs`: a rung exactly at the top of the work is dropped.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/2004-top-z-level.md` (items 3 and 4d are now decided).

Posted G-code changes: each depth-stepping operation that uses the level law cuts one level fewer (the air level at Top Z), unless stock stands over Top Z. Then the program keeps the old levels. The bore-side helix transition of the first level now starts 2 mm (plunge height) over the top of the cut. This is under the safety floor.


## Round 5 (head `b18b928131467a963022f3efcd6bc6352fd07599`)

The lanes of 2D Adaptive (Trochoidal) copy it from the pocket links. Decision item 9.

title: fix(2d): Side Auto reads the material at the picked ring's own level
body:
The base is `main`. #1935 is merged (`cfc8447ee`), and this branch has `origin/main` merged in (`6bbed2171`).

## What changed

- Side Auto of a 2D Contour on picked rings now reads the part section at the rings' own level. It does not read the full XY silhouette. The floor of a blind bore filled that silhouette, so Auto resolved Outside on the bore rim and the #1927 law refused the pass.
- New law `machining2d::auto_side` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_auto.rs`):
  - It reads the section 0.01 mm under the top of the picks' Z span, then 0.01 mm over its bottom.
  - At each probe it compares the area inside the rings with a 0.5 mm band outside the rings. A side holds material at a fill of 0.5 or more.
  - Material inside only gives Outside. Material outside only gives Inside. The first probe that decides is the result.
  - If the two probes decide differently, or if they see material on both sides and do not decide, the generate is refused by name: "Side Auto cannot tell which side of the picked ring holds the material at Z ...: ... - set Side to Inside or Outside".
  - If no probe sees material on either side (a sheet part, a ring over the part in air), the part's XY outline decides, as before.
- New `crates/app/src/operation/contour_auto_pick.rs`: it reads the Z span of the picks (in the setup frame, or along a tilted frame's axis) and the material, and calls the law.
- `selection.rs` uses the new verdict in place of the old fill block. `generate.rs` refuses an Undecided verdict by name. `contour_auto_side` (the UI preview) maps Undecided to "no answer".
- The rule applies only to `OpParams::Contour` with Side Auto. Plasma and wire contours do not use this verdict.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1933-contour-auto-side-level.md`.

## Readings (tool centre to the wall, Ø6 tool, Side Auto, model top to model bottom)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Blind bore rim, Ø20 bore to floor Z 4, rim at Z 10 | Outside, refused "set Side to Inside" | Inside, centre 3.000 mm inside the wall (max error 0.000001), deepest level Z 4.000 (the floor), 0 gouges |
| Same bore, floor rim at Z 4 | Outside | Inside, same pass, deepest level Z 4.000, 0 gouges |
| Through hole Ø20 | Inside | Inside, centre 3.000 mm inside the wall, cut to Z 0, 0 gouges |
| Boss 20 x 20 on a floor at Z 5 | Outside | Outside, centre 3.000 mm outside the wall, cut to Z 5, 0 gouges |
| Block 40 x 40 outer wall | Outside | Outside, centre 3.000 mm outside the wall, cut to Z 0, 0 gouges |
| `Milling-test.step` bore rim r 12.5 at Z 20 (Ø10 tool) | Outside, refused | Inside, the same moves as Side Inside, centre 5.000 mm inside the rim, 0 warnings |

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/contour_auto_level.rs` (new, 3 tests): `auto_on_a_blind_bore_rim_cuts_the_wall_from_inside_to_the_floor`, `auto_on_a_through_hole_rim_cuts_inside`, `auto_on_a_boss_and_on_an_outer_wall_cuts_outside`.
- `crates/motion/tests/contour_auto_side.rs` (new, 6 tests): the law on boxes, the floor rim, the mid-solid refusal, the disagreeing probes refusal, the outline fallback and the empty part.
- `crates/app/tests/area_open.rs`: `a_containment_that_puts_the_tool_in_the_part_is_refused_by_name`. Its last assert now expects the clean Inside pass in place of the refusal.
- The #1935 refusals are unchanged: `contour_outside_hole` 5 of 5 pass.
- `operations.rs` 120 pass, 6 ignored. This includes the sheet-part tests `contour_boss_pick_defaults_outside`, `a_closed_chain_routes_the_boundary_path_not_a_centerline` and `selection_notes_report_stitching_and_extension`.

## Gate

Gate on head `6bbed21715b726e96ac39430b945e15e72bdc89f` (this branch with `origin/main` merged in, no hand edits in the merge). The touched test binaries ran one by one (debug, `-j 6`, `--test-threads=6`):

| Crate | Binary | Result |
|---|---|---|
| camcraft-app | `setup_align` | 10 pass |
| camcraft-app | `stitch_cross` | 6 pass |
| camcraft-app | `contour_auto_level` | 3 pass |
| camcraft-app | `area_open` | 11 pass |
| camcraft-app | `contour_outside_hole` | 5 pass |
| camcraft-app | `operations` | 120 pass, 6 ignored |
| camcraft-motion | `contour_auto_side` | 6 pass |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings` is clean.

The 2 app tests that were red on the old head `13a1f2625` now pass:
- `setup_align::unverified_kinds_are_refused_while_verified_picks_generate_aligned`
- `stitch_cross::a_self_touching_single_body_still_stops_at_its_top_level`

Cause: the old head was based on an earlier #1935 head. The last #1935 commit `72c8f293d` (now on main) changed these 2 tests for the #1927 refusal law, and changed `contour_depth.rs` to name an unreadable mesh. The merge of `origin/main` brought in that commit. This PR changes no assert of these 2 tests.

Earlier full quick gate on `13a1f2625` (36.6 min): post ok, motion ok, ui ok, app failed only in the 2 tests above.

- Side Auto under a tilted frame (the code reads the frame's local facets; no test).

- Plasma and wire contours: the verdict is not used there. They lose the note "machining inside the ring - the selection bounds air", which they did not act on.

The merge had no conflicts. Git merged 3 files that both sides changed: `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs` and `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`. The app binaries above and clippy cover the merged result of these files.

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket operation
body:
Fork synced at v0.20.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 71).

## What changed

The 2D Pocket can now cut only what a larger previous tool left. It uses the rest generator of #1446 (`machining2d::rest_pocket`).

- **Parameter.** `OpParams::Pocket` has a new optional `rest` group: previous tool diameter, its corner radius, the stock it left on the walls, and the rest allowance. `None` is off. Off is the default and the plain pocket.
- **Undoable edit.** You change the group through `EditOperationParams`. Undo and redo restore it.
- **Project file.** The key is `rest` (an object). A file without the key reads as off, so the file version does not change.
- **Stamp.** The stamp writes the group (byte `0xD7`) only when it is on. Each value of the group changes the stamp.
- **Generation.** When the group is on, generation calls `rest_pocket`. Its note ("rest machining trusts the entered previous tool ...") goes into the path notes.
- **Refusals by name, in the generator's own words, when you make, edit or retool the operation** (not only at Generate):
  - a previous tool that is not larger than the operation's tool (new `rest_gate`, run from `tool_gate` and from the edit);
  - a value that is negative or not finite, a previous tool diameter that is 0 or less, or a corner radius larger than the previous tool's radius;
  - the Zigzag or Adaptive strategy;
  - pre-drilled entry with rest machining on (`REST_PREDRILLED`). `rest_pocket` does not read the holes, and the program must not drop a user setting without saying so.
- **Motion crate.** `RestParams` has a new `validate_alone` (the checks that do not need a tool, plus "the previous tool diameter must be positive"). The strategy check moved into a public `rest_strategy`. Its text did not change.
- **MCP.** `edit_operation` sets the group (`"rest": null` turns it off). There is a new row in the camcraft-mcp skill. Area: mcp.
- **Not in this PR: the dialog group.** It is not part of "Done means", and it needs before/after screenshots and the UI gate. The page keeps the group as it is when you apply the page. Follow-up: #1815.

## How tested

The new pinning tests are in `crates/app/tests/rest_pocket.rs`:
- `the_rest_pass_cuts_only_the_corners_posts_and_matches_its_golden`: the fixture is a 60 x 40 pocket with 3 mm corners. A 12 mm end mill roughs it, then a 4 mm end mill does the rest pass. The golden is `pocket_rest_corners.cl`. All cuts stay in the corners. The program posts and the verification report is clean.
- `read_against_the_simulated_roughing_pass`: the roughing pass is simulated first on the stock dexel grid. Then:
  - no rapid of the rest pass hits stock;
  - every plunge goes down on floor that is already clear, and its rim touches stock for no more than one level;
  - all 8 rings (4 corners x 2 levels) cut stock, and air is less than half of each ring.
- `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_and_the_project_file_keeps_it`
- `a_previous_tool_that_is_not_larger_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_the_retool` (edit, create and retool)
- `values_and_strategies_the_rest_pass_cannot_run_are_refused_by_name`
- `mcp_sets_refuses_undoes_and_saves_the_group` (set, refuse, save, reopen, null, undo)

Other tests:
- `operation::rest_op_tests::the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`
- `crates/motion/tests/rest2d.rs`: a new case for a 0 mm previous tool.

Mutation check: I deleted each new refusal line, the stamp line and the generation line one at a time, ran the test that pins it, and saw it fail. Then I restored the file and compared it with a backup. All 11 failed when deleted and were restored byte for byte: the motion "must be positive" check, rest_op's three refusals, sane's `named_refusal` and `is_sane` lines, `rest_gate` in `tool_gate`, `rest_gate` in the edit, the refusal arm inside `rest_gate`, the `0xD7` stamp block, and the `rest_pocket` call in generation.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick` plans almost the whole workspace for this diff, so I ran the touched suites by name instead (motion: lib, rest2d, machining2d, predrilled_entry, corner_arc_radius, optimal_load, solid_law; app: lib, rest_pocket, golden_cl, arc_turn_params, predrilled_entry, project_roundtrip, roughing2d, adaptive_trochoid, mcp, mcp_pockets, pocket_recognition, operations, commands_undo, tool_gate, tool_law, verify, solid_law_goldens, heights, tilt, corner_blend, climb_direction, area_controls, pick_agnostic, pocket_overhead, units_in_refusals, lead_approach, level_links, whole_model_pocket, recorded_post_streams; ui: lib, edge_loop_pick, operations). All green. Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-motion, camcraft-app and camcraft-ui (all targets): clean.

The existing pocket goldens do not change (`golden_cl`, `adaptive_trochoid`, `roughing2d` and the others in the list above).

## What I did not test

- I did not run the program on a machine, and I did not take screenshots (there is no UI change).
- Two things I measured but did not fix, because they are generator behaviour and not part of this slice:
  - The inner leg of each corner ring crosses floor that the 12 mm tool already cleared: 6.7 mm of a 14.8-15.3 mm ring. Follow-up: #1816.
  - On each level, 2 of the 4 corner plunges touch rest material at the rim. The tool axis is over cleared floor. Entry from cleared space belongs to #1490.
- All of these are feed moves, so they cost time, not safety.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1489-rest-pocket-param.md`.

body:
Adds the finish3d `gap_link` parameter: a dropdown with `Jump` (default, today's retract/clearance hop, unchanged) and `Straight` (one straight Feed link between the run ends at their own tip height - no rise, no traverse, no plunge).

What changed:
- `camcraft_motion::finishing3d`: new `GapLink` enum (default `Jump`) and `Finish3DParams.gap_link`; new `gaplink.rs` with the `Straight` verdict; the `emit_runs` chain tries the straight link on a break the `ramp` diagonal refused, and keeps the plain hop when the verdict says no.
- The law: the line is fixed (both run ends are legal tangent centers by the march's own construction), so the exact segment-triangle sweep of the move at the budget `r - TOUCH_EPS` answers the whole question. Grazing rims pass, a real bite refuses, and a refusal takes the `Jump` hop byte for byte as every older file ran.
- Serpentine fix: a raster line broken by openings now runs back WHOLE (`pieces.reverse()` plus each piece's points). Reversing only the points made every gap link jump back across the whole field instead of crossing its gap. This shortens the existing `Jump` traverses on broken lines too.
- Project file: the words `jump` and `straight`, written always like `ramp` - no version step-up; older files read as `jump`. The digest takes tag `0x4D` plus a variant byte only when the choice is not `Jump`, so ops that hop as before keep their old stamp.
- UI: "Gap link" combo (Jump / Straight) in the Mill 3D passes section. MCP: the same words ride the existing `edit_operation` params door and undo.

How tested: `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_gaplink.rs` - 6 pins: the jump pin (byte-for-byte old behavior), straight links over a holed plate at the run height, every straight link kept clear of the facets (exact sweep scan, Prime Directive), straight refused over a biting slot keeps the plain hop (byte-for-byte `Jump` crossings), and every hop traverse spans one gap, never the field (fails on the pre-fix serpentine with a 31.7 mm field jump). Round-trip pins in `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs` (jump/straight/absent) and the params-door test in `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs`. GUI check: the maintainer approved the two-option surface (`Jump` as before, `Straight` as here) in chat after testing the Straight link over the holes in his 171 mm STEP part on an intermediate build; the `Straight` law itself is unchanged in this rebuild. A release build of this head is available for a re-test.
